blocks.md: A **settlement** is a place where people live and work, from a small hamlet to a big city. The **site** is the actual land on which the settlement is built; the **situation** is its position in relation to the land around it (roads, rivers, other towns). People choose sites with a **water supply**, **flat or gently sloping land**, **fertile soil**, safety from floods and enemies, building materials, and good routes.

blocks.caption: Three settlement patterns
blocks.alt: Three small diagrams of houses: grouped together, in a line along a road, and scattered apart.

blocks.title: Rural and urban
blocks.md: **Rural** settlements (villages, hamlets) are small, with most people farming, fishing or herding. **Urban** settlements (towns, cities) are large, with most people working in trade, services, offices and industries, and with many services such as hospitals, schools and markets.

blocks.title: Patterns
blocks.md:
- **Nucleated**: houses grouped closely round a centre such as a market or a spring.
- **Linear**: houses in a line along a road, river or coast.
- **Dispersed**: houses far apart, scattered, often among farms.

Towns have **functions**, the main jobs they do. **Douala** is a port and commercial centre. **Yaoundé** is the capital, with government offices and universities. **Garoua** is a river port on the Benue and a regional centre in the north. **Limbe** is a coastal town with a port, tourism and an oil refinery. Many towns have a mixture of functions. Settlements often grow along main roads and at river crossings.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Site and situation are different: site = the land itself; situation = relationship to surroundings.
- A big village is still rural if people mostly farm; size is not the only difference.
- Settlement patterns are general descriptions: real places often mix them.

blocks.title: Example 1: site factors
blocks.statement: A new village is planned near a stream on a gentle slope with good soil. Give two reasons why this is a good site.
steps: The stream gives a water supply for drinking and farming.
A gentle slope avoids flooding and is easy to build on.
blocks.answer: Water supply and gentle, well-drained land (and fertile soil).

blocks.title: Example 2: pattern
blocks.statement: Houses stand one after another along the main road from Kumba towards Mamfe, with farms behind them. Which pattern is this?
steps: The houses follow a single line.
The line is controlled by the road.
